working_title: County Down's Golf Circuit: A Practical Guide to Playing Royal County Down, Ardglass and Kirkistown Castle
angle: County Down is home to one of the world's great links in Royal County Down, but with visitor tee times there scarce and green fees now at £450 a round, the savvy UK golfer needs a plan that also folds in Ardglass and Kirkistown Castle — two genuinely brilliant alternatives that reward the detour and leave money in the pocket for the ferry home.
research_notes:
- Royal County Down, Newcastle, County Down: par 71 Championship Links, 7,186 yards, set between the Mountains of Mourne and Dundrum Bay / Irish Sea. Also has the shorter Annesley Links (par 66, 4,548 yards). Founded 1889. Consistently ranked in the world's top 5 courses.
- RCD visitor green fees 2026: Championship Links £450 peak season (per wanderinggolfers.com / nationalclubgolfer.com 2026 survey). Annesley Links significantly cheaper (low-to-mid £40s range cited by multiple sources — confirm on royalcountydown.org before publishing).
- RCD visitor days: typically Mon, Tue, Thu morning, Fri, Sun afternoon — NOT Wednesday (confirm with club). Advance booking essential. Handicap required (24 for men, 36 for ladies per one source — verify on club site).
- RCD sits within Murlough Nature Reserve; the course layout zigzags back and forth offering varying vistas throughout the round.
- Ardglass Golf Club, Ardglass village, ~28–30 miles south of Belfast, ~30 mins from RCD. 18-hole links, par 70, approx 6,268 yards. Clinging to the Irish Sea coast, front holes hug cliff edges. Opens with a short uphill par 4 described as one of the most dramatic opening tee shots in golf.
- Ardglass green fees (guide prices, verify with club): midweek approx £115, weekends approx £135–£140. Much more accessible than RCD.
- Ardglass clubhouse: Ardglass Castle, parts dating to 1405 — widely claimed to be the oldest golf clubhouse in the world (the club acknowledges rival claimants exist, including Varese in Italy). Houses Restaurant 1405.
- Ardglass halfway house: cottage at rear of 7th green, noted for a pint and sea views — a distinctive and well-loved feature.
- Ardglass ranked 41st in Ireland by Irish Golfer 2026, 165th in GB&I by Golf World 2026. Green fees have risen sharply as word spread — peak-season fee was cited as £220 in 2025 by one US-focused source (GolfPass), but UK-facing sources (Golfshake, where2golf) quote £115 midweek / £135–£140 weekends — treat pricing as indicative and direct readers to club website.
- Kirkistown Castle Golf Club, Cloughey, Ards Peninsula. Founded 1902; course significantly shaped by James Braid in 1934. Par 70, 6,167 yards (white tees). 18-hole links.
- Kirkistown is the nearest links to Belfast (~45 mins via A20 through Newtownards) and the most easterly 18-hole course on the island of Ireland.
- Recently recognised as 'Best Value Golf Experience in Ulster'. Quick-draining links — rarely closed after rain. Visitors welcome every day, advance booking essential.
- Green fees at Kirkistown: one source quotes £40 per 18 holes (1golf.eu) — treat as indicative; verify with club.
- Practice facilities at Kirkistown: practice ground, two putting greens, pitching green, practice nets.
- Getting there: Belfast has two airports (George Best Belfast City and Belfast International). Ferries to Belfast from Cairnryan (Scotland, ~2hrs 20min sailing) and from Liverpool — good options for UK visitors bringing a car.
- RCD handicap restrictions: 24 (men) / 36 (ladies) on Championship Course — one source reference; direct readers to verify on club site.
- Slieve Donard Resort & Spa in Newcastle is the well-known hotel base for RCD rounds — informational mention only, no affiliate link unless pre-approved.
- Clandeboye Golf Club (Conlig, near Bangor) also worth a mention as a strong parkland/heathland option near Belfast: 36 holes (Dufferin Championship course, par 71, 6,742 yards; shorter Ava course). Visitor green fees: Dufferin ~£70–£90 midweek, ~£80–£100 weekends (multiple sources, slight variance — treat as indicative). Good warm-up or add-on round for those flying into Belfast.
must_avoid:
- Do not fabricate specific green fees as confirmed prices — cite all fees as approximate/guide prices and direct readers to book directly with each club for current rates, as figures vary between sources.
- Do not claim the Ardglass clubhouse IS definitively the world's oldest — the club itself notes rival claimants; reflect that nuance.
- No invented quotes from pros, reviewers or club staff.
- No affiliate links for Slieve Donard or any accommodation/travel operator unless confirmed in approved-partners list — mention informally with no link.
- Do not give Wednesday as an available visitor day at RCD without confirming with the club — one source explicitly states RCD does not permit visitors on Wednesdays.
- No gambling/betting content, no medical/injury advice, no financial affordability advice.
- No em dashes anywhere in the post.
- UK English throughout (favour, colour, -ise endings).
- Do not duplicate angles from the southwest-ireland-golf-circuit or scotland-s-angus-links posts — this is Northern Ireland / County Down specific.
